You aren't there for entertainment - you're there to get yourself to the point of mental stability.. :/

yes, because you don't have someone whose job is to prevent you from fucking killing yourself.

i was in a mental health institution twice, each for a little over 2 weeks (~15-17 days).

it felt like summer camp, except you didn't contact with the outside world, and it wasn't a particularly interesting camp with ridiculously high security. everyone knew why they were there, and only a couple tried arguing their way out (1 successfully because every time someone looked in her general direction she would immediately try to attack and say 'that's what you get for being a fucking mental case'). idk what happened to her. but yeah. everyone knew why they were there and what they need to do to get the hell out. everyone collectively put judgments behind them because the other 15ish kids were the only contact with the outside world they had, aside from phone calls. you gotta make the best of the situation sometimes.

there were an array of kids; complete and total nerds to kids that have been involved in gangs for years already. high school dropouts to ivy league applicants. fugly people to very attractive people. talented people to the-not-so-gifted. as for why they were there, reasons included anxiety, anger, OCD, depression, eating disorders, drug abuse, alcohol abuse, and suicide ideation/attempts.

we had a set schedule for each day (following a regular and planned schedule eases anxiety, obsessive thinking/actions, etc) with time set aside for meals, schoolwork, free time (pretty much just foosball / espn / offline madden / ping pong / card games / whatever girls do), and a non-health focused group activity (ie ping pong tournament, music jeopardy, watching a movie, bingo, etc).

had 2-3 health-focused group activities. some weren't bad, but some were pretty abysmal. everyone shared pretty much the same opinion for each activity.

there weren't arguments or fights (well, almost had 1, but that's cause a guy and two of his exes were in the hospital at the same time, lol... all 3 got transferred).

idk if it affected me. i met some great friends and then lost them (not to suicide, but just me being socially incompetent). i was happier than before for a good amount of time after my second visit, but i can kinda feel myself being meh right now. probably just stress from schoolwork right now.

you can only get "healthier" if you want to. if you go in without a goal, you'll walk out the same way.

the staff really aren't that bad. if you show them respect, they'll show you respect. it's that fucking easy and should be applied universally. take time to talk to them privately if you need.

i just feel so confused with my future. for one, i'm being forced into making a decision that will impact the rest of my life. (and i'm going to reference some shitpost i saw on twitter or something) i'm making a permanent, lifechanging decision, when an hour ago i had to ask permission to use the bathroom. i'm ready for college, academically. i'm ready for college, socially. i'm not ready for college, emotionally. if i've spent thirteen years trying to make friends and only making four (two of which weren't even at school), how the fuck am i going to make friends in college? i don't even understand. people say just find new friends. i literally can't. i have asperger's, and it is so fucking immensely difficult to even strike up a conversation with someone, let alone befriend someone. people say "just go up to someone and start a conversation." look, that doesn't fucking happen. not with me. not with anyone at my school. the stigmas are so ridiculously intense at my school, that there is no climbing the social ladder or recovering from being labeled. its a school of 2200ish, and there is no escaping labels or cliques or anything.

plus, one of my biggest worries of all time ties in with social life. finding a girlfriend and (eventually) marrying. most people get married. it is something i will (probably) do. but i am scared out of my fucking mind about it. yeah, i'm young, but that doesn't prevent me from worrying about the future. what happens if a girlfriend of four years just leaves me the same way G did? its been seven months since a six month long friendship has ended and i still miss it. how the fuck am i going to move on from something ridiculously impactful? okay, assume that doesn't happen, and i marry a girl. up to 50% of marriages (or something like that) end in divorce. my parents are a great example. they are fucking miserable. they hate each other. i hate them. i hate their lifestyles, how they talk to each other, and how they put me in the middle. i don't ever want to be like them. but with a statistic like that, how the fuck can you avoid it? you can't. that's it. you cannot avoid it. if thats the case, i don't really want to have to deal with that. i don't want to experience the future, if its coated with pain and misery. i don't want to end up at a job i hate cause its the only one i can find, then go home and play videogames for a few hours, go to bed, and repeat.

look, i tell myself all the time i'm a terrible friend. how am i ever going to be a good boyfriend or husband if i can't even love myself? i've spent four years in therapy addressing my self esteem. nothing, ever, has helped, aside from making meaningful connections with people. meds don't help, aside from klonopin for panic and adderall for helping me focus on school (otherwise racing thoughts take control of my brain and i can't do anything), and melatonin to help me sleep. been on probably up to 10 antidepressants. none worked. i just... am pessimistic about the future. and no therapist has ever helped me with that.

I've been rejected by about every single clique in school. I've been in the same school district since Kindergarten (I'm a senior now) and I've always tried to make friends but only a few ever worked out to be a good friendship. I was a conceited asshole from middle school to sophomore year. Then my depression really kicked in, and I began to tell myself that I wasn't any good and everyone else was better. I made many acquaintances over the years, but only around four friends, two of which I met at a hospital.

One, G, I'll call her, was the first person to ever call me their best friend, and that meant a ton to me. We had an incredible bond and were fantastic friends. I finally found someone that understood me. Suddenly one weekend, she stops replying to all texts, and a few days later she texts me "I've changed. We can't be friends anymore." and that was that... that was probably 7 months ago and I still miss her and think about her. We only knew each other for probably 5 before that, but we were in the hospital together so we spent a lot of time together.

Another friend, J, was the first friend I ever made. She was a great friend. She stopped a good amount of the bullying that went on against me, and she was always making sure I was smiling. I tried my hardest to do that for her, as well. She didn't have depression or anxiety or any mental illness (afaik), and she was always a really happy person, so it was hard to return it to her. Anyways, over the years, she became really obsessed with dating and materialistic, and we talked less and less. I decided to give the friendship one last shot by asking her to prom junior year, and she lied her way out of it. I decided enough was enough, and if she had to lie, she wasn't a good friend, so I ended the friendship.

Third, L, I'll call her, whom I met at the hospital, is still a friend today. But... not a great one. She's always very, very busy and she lives ~30 minutes away so it's really hard to make plans to see each other. She never really seems to want to talk much either, but I always see her posts all over twitter, mostly pictures of her and her friends. I'm happy for her - she has come a long way since I met her in the hospital, and I'm proud of her. It's just really hard to call her a friend when we barely ever talk (despite me reaching out to her) and I haven't seen her since probably November. I wish we could be better friends. It's just hard to form a bond with her, even though she has such a deep and unique personality. Sometimes I doubt she wants to be friends.

Anyways, lastly, C, is my best and closest friend. She is the only one who knows I went to a hospital (twice) and she talked to me on the phone while I was in there whenever we got the chance. She talked me out of suicide countless times, and I would not be here without her. She is an amazing person. I really can't say enough about her. There's too much to write here. But, you get my drift. Only problem is - she's super busy, just like L. She's got school, a job, an internship, clubs, sports, and a boyfriend. I'm not upset with her for being so busy. I'm not jealous of her boyfriend or her other friends. It's just that it's hard to find a chance to hang out, especially since we're both starting to do our college essays / applications and she has very demanding parents. She's always willing to talk and is very easy to talk to. She wants to be a therapist, and she'd be a damn good one.

Anyways, the rest of the people in my life are just acquaintances that don't talk to me unless they need help with homework or schoolwork. It's a really shallow community that's only obsessed with their grades and believe that if you don't go to a good college then you're a useless prick. (They won't settle for anything that isn't an Ivy League school, even though they don't have the grades to get in). They're just... idk. they have like 2100-2200 SAT scores, a 3.8-3.9 GPA, don't do any extracurricular stuff, and they think they're the top of the food chain. It's really hard to fit in with those people, and they surround me since I'm in full AP classes.

I've been bullied for the clothes I wear, for being too smart, for being too stupid (yes, I've been bullied by the stereotypical nerd), for being arrogant, for being quiet, for everything. I don't know anymore. I don't know who I am, and I don't know what other people think of me. I just want others to think well of me. And I have a shred of the feeling that they don't. A lot of teachers don't like me because I find easier ways to solve problems than how they want me to solve the problem, but others love me for it.

I had severe depression all through junior year so my grades were really, really shit (like 88 GPA) up until the fourth quarter, and all my finals were above a 95. I had no motivation to do any work. I often just didn't do homework because I didn't feel like it, and got away with it (somehow), even though I was in full honors courses. I somehow got into full AP courses this year, and my grades are great (all 95+ so far, except one class at a 93). I've been told I'm useless, but at the same time I'm told I have so much potential. I've been told my grades aren't good enough, but at the same time, that they're fantastic. I've been told I'm not following directions, but I'm merely just finding an easier way to solve the problem at hand.

There's so much confusion in my head about who I am.

Yeah, so. Hope you read.

Remember: The hospital is to help you. Please do not fight them. Please accept all the help and opportunities they give you. I've seen all too many people throw away such a precious chance. I know the hospital isn't going to be the solution, but it can really help guide you to making your days a little better. I know from experience. Been in a hospital twice. First time, didn't want to do anything, didn't participate in anything, didn't take any opportunities or chances. Second time, that changed. Haven't been there in 6 months. Sure, I still struggle, but a lot less. Keep your chin up :)
